newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close softer in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close softer in directionless trade.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended lower on Tuesday in directionless trading as individual heavyweight stocks dominated.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slipped 5.13 points to 6532.34, hovering below the all-time high of 6557.03 set on Monday.
"It's kind of a special situation market today," said Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram.
Conglomerate Canadian Pacific Ltd. jumped in heavy trading after Monday's news that it sold its substantial stake in Laidlaw Inc. worth C$1 billion ($722 million).
CP owned 47 percent of the transportation and waste management company's class A shares and 11 percent of its class B shares.
Canadian Pacific gained 1.75 to reach a new 52-week high of 39.80.
Laidlaw's class B shares rose 0.25 to 19.10 and topped Toronto's most actives at 3.2 million shares while its class A shares jumped 2.05 to hit a one-year record of 21.10 in light trading.

But Ram warned that Toronto's market will not be able to sustain its lofty levels as investors become nervous and decide to sell to take profits after recent gains. "We're on a limited fuse," he said.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes dropped, nearly offset by five soaring sectors. The weaker side was led by golds, consumer products, media and base metals.
Conglomerates spiralled up 3.3 percent aided by CP's strength, followed by transportation and oils.
Trading was moderate at 80.9 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1.0 billion).
Declining issues beat out advances 520 to 470 while 297 ended flat.

In other issues, Emco Ltd. slipped 1.15 to 15.40 in turnover of nearly 460,000 shares. The building materials maker said on Tuesday it will issue C$75 million ($54 million) worth of 6.5 percent convertible subordinated debentures.
